item.text:
I would harden three areas.

`averageItemPrice` in [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:17) needs a defined empty-input behavior. Right now, once `calcTotal` is fixed, `[]` would produce `NaN` or `Infinity` depending on how it evolves. That should either return `0` or throw a clear error.

`averageItemPrice` also has a semantics problem. It currently computes `sum(price * qty) / items.length`, which is average line total, not average item price in the usual sense. If callers expect average unit price, the result is wrong. I would either rename it or change the formula after clarifying intent.

The module assumes all item fields are present and numeric. In [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:5), [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:22), and [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:23), bad input like missing `price`, missing `qty`, or a non-array `items` will still throw or produce `NaN`. Even lightweight validation would make failures predictable and easier to debug.

Less critical, but I’d also decide whether `applyDiscount` should normalize codes like `save10` or trim whitespace. Right now it silently ignores anything not matching exact uppercase keys, which may be fine, but it is a deliberate API choice rather than a robust default.
